record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Does Baire space have a degree of topological categoricity?

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Does the Baire space have a degree of categoricity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $\mathcal{N} = \omega^\omega$ denote the Baire space, i.e. the set of all functions from $\omega$ to $\omega$ equipped with the product topology (with $\omega$ discrete). A computable (Polish) presentation of a Polish space $X$ is a pair consisting of a countable dense sequence $(x_i)_{i\in\omega}$ in $X$ together with a complete compatible metric $d$ such that the function $(i,j)\mapsto d(x_i,x_j)$ is computable as a real-valued function (uniformly in $i,j$). Given a Turing degree $\mathbf{d}$, two computable presentations of $X$ are said to be $\mathbf{d}$-homeomorphic if there is a homeomorphism between the underlying spaces that, regarded as a map between Cauchy-name representations, is computable relative to an oracle of degree $\mathbf{d}$.

A Turing degree $\mathbf{d}$ is called a degree of topological categoricity of a Polish space $X$ if:
(i) for any two computable presentations of $X$ there is a $\mathbf{d}$-computable homeomorphism between them; and
(ii) $\mathbf{d}$ is the least such degree (i.e. every degree $\mathbf{e}$ satisfying (i) also satisfies $\mathbf{d}\le_T \mathbf{e}$).

Question. Does the Baire space $\mathcal{N} = \omega^\omega$ admit a degree of topological categoricity?

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether Polish spaces (and in particular the Baire space) admit degrees of topological categoricity is part of an actively investigated but largely unresolved area. Surveys on computable categoricity of Polish spaces describe this as a "wide open area," and no published resolution for the Baire-space case was located. Status appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Computable categoricity of Polish spaces (search summary)
status_evidence.snippet: Computable categoricity of effectively compact Polish spaces and Polish groups up to computable homeomorphism is a wide open area.
status_evidence.claim: Computable categoricity for Polish spaces, of which Baire space is the canonical example, is described as wide open.

status_evidence.title: Degrees of categoricity above 0 — Dino Rossegger
status_evidence.snippet: Strong degrees of categoricity above 0'' classified as treeable degrees — degrees of Turing least paths through computable trees in Baire space.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on degrees of categoricity uses Baire space, but the question of whether Baire space itself has a (topological) degree of categoricity is not addressed as solved.
